partial.not_covered: A location is "targeted" when an active schedule names it. Range → location mapping beyond the schedule's own location is not derived; ITOM-004 (schedules with no location) makes this rule's answer unverifiable.

A successful discovery is read as a device-history row that produced a CI (cmdb_ci set); the phase outcome itself is not established. Current network CI data is taken as CI IP addresses.

a device-type inference from port signatures and partial classification — the workbook names the idea, not the signature → type mapping
owned by PLT-139 (ownership OWN-005, proposed owner PLT-139): the vault condition is evaluated once, in the Platform catalogue (Phase 6)

partial.not_covered: "No schedule reference" cannot be judged — schedules do not reference credentials (see ITOM-018) — so only the no-successful-use half is evaluated; the rule can fail but never pass.
The configured window is the schedule's max run; a schedule without one is not judged. The trend is an ordinary least-squares line through run durations.
"Truncated" has no platform state of its own; a run is truncated here when it outlasted its schedule's max run.
"Within the interval" is not applied — any later completed run counts as a re-run; the cancelling user is not shown.

the pattern versions ServiceNow ships with each instance family — external reference data

The workbook's fallback — comparing host identifiers — is used; resolution through the CMDB host and hypervisor relationships is not.
The instance's version is read as its mid.version property (the build its MIDs should run) and compared whole, which is stricter than "major and minor".

partial.not_covered: The impact tree is stored per CI (em_impact_status.element_id → business_service), not per alert: a Critical alert counts as having an affected service when its bound CI's impact tree names one.
Each active em_alert notification's condition is evaluated by the instance (D-033 (docs/HEALTH-ASSIST-RULE-RESEARCH.md)); a notification fired by an event or a flow is not seen.
Each active alert management rule's alert_filter is evaluated by the instance against the alerts retained (D-033 (docs/HEALTH-ASSIST-RULE-RESEARCH.md)).
The events are those each retained alert absorbed (em_alert.event_count, D-033 (docs/HEALTH-ASSIST-RULE-RESEARCH.md)), so both counts share the alert's retention window.
Critical = em_alert severity 1; an incident-creating rule is an alert management rule of type "incident", whose alert_filter the instance evaluates (D-033 (docs/HEALTH-ASSIST-RULE-RESEARCH.md)).
Correlated by message key (the dedup key); the node half of the key is not compared.

partial.not_covered: Deletions are the platform's deleted-record audit (sys_audit_delete) for cmdb_rel_ci, attributed to a discovery run that did not complete when they fall between its start and its last update. Deletions older than the audit retention are not seen.

A Business Critical service with no impact tree (em_impact_graph), its model walked down as CSDM-075 does; where it reaches the application or infrastructure layer, the break point is traced to Service Mapping (a mapped service with no CI), a CI never discovered (no discovery source) or discovery issues on the CI (D-037). Other ITOM findings are not joined; a model ending higher is CSDM-075's.

N: CIs in the discovery history of the schedule's runs that have no location; M: assignment (routing), alert management and event rules whose conditions name a location, by name (D-037). "DR" rules are not a platform object and are not counted; a location set later by a pattern (the guard) is read as the CI stands now.
